reference.source: Resnick's Diagnosis of Bone and Joint Disorders / GeneReviews
clinicalPearls: Defined by the combination of cutaneous connective-tissue naevi (elastomas rich in elastin, or collagenomas) with the spotty sclerotic bone lesions of osteopoikilosis
Skin lesions are typically firm, skin-coloured or yellowish papules and plaques, often on the trunk and limbs, and may be present from childhood
Shares the same causal gene as isolated osteopoikilosis, LEMD3, so the two conditions represent a spectrum with variable cutaneous expression
Autosomal dominant inheritance with marked intrafamilial variability means some relatives show only skin lesions and others only bone findings
The bone foci are asymptomatic incidental findings and, like osteopoikilosis, show no increased scintigraphic uptake
Skin biopsy of a naevus confirms disorganised or increased dermal elastin/collagen and supports the diagnosis
Management is reassurance; skin lesions may be removed for cosmetic reasons but this is not medically necessary
reference.pathophysiology: Buschke-Ollendorff syndrome is caused by heterozygous loss-of-function variants in LEMD3, the same inner nuclear membrane protein implicated in osteopoikilosis, which normally restrains bone morphogenetic protein and transforming growth factor-beta signalling. In this disorder the dysregulated signalling manifests in both mesenchymal tissues: the dermis develops connective-tissue naevi with excess or disordered elastic and collagen fibres, while the skeleton develops the scattered sclerotic enostosis-like foci of osteopoikilosis. The variable balance of skin and bone involvement within a single family reflects the pleiotropic effect of the shared genetic defect rather than distinct disorders.
additionalDifferentials: Tuberous sclerosis (shagreen patch and sclerotic bone islands)
Isolated connective-tissue naevus or nevus lipomatosus
Osteoblastic skeletal metastases (radiographic mimic of the bone foci)
Focal dermal hypoplasia and other elastic-tissue disorders
additionalInvestigations: Skin examination and biopsy of a representative papule for elastin and collagen assessment
Plain radiographs or skeletal survey demonstrating the osteopoikilosis-type foci
Bone scintigraphy where malignancy needs to be excluded
LEMD3 molecular genetic testing to confirm the diagnosis
Family assessment including skin examination and targeted imaging of relatives
Dermatological photography to document and monitor cutaneous lesions
redFlags: New focal bone pain or a lesion with cortical destruction or increased uptake, prompting exclusion of metastatic disease
Rapidly changing or ulcerating skin lesion atypical for a benign connective-tissue naevus
Family history of a severe or unexplained bone disorder warranting broader evaluation
reference.prognosis: The syndrome is benign with a normal life expectancy; both the skin naevi and bone foci are harmless, and the principal risk is unnecessary intervention prompted by misdiagnosis of the sclerotic lesions as malignancy.
pitfalls: Interpreting the sclerotic bone foci as osteoblastic metastases and triggering an unwarranted oncological workup
Failing to link coexisting skin naevi and bone lesions, thereby missing the unifying diagnosis
Overlooking the autosomal dominant inheritance and the need to counsel and examine relatives
Assuming the skin lesions require aggressive treatment when observation is appropriate
references: Resnick's Diagnosis of Bone and Joint Disorders
management: Reassure the patient and avoid unnecessary intervention, recognising the sclerotic bone foci as benign osteopoikilosis-type lesions to prevent misdiagnosis as osteoblastic metastases
Manage asymptomatic bone lesions conservatively, as they require no specific treatment
Confirm the diagnosis with skin biopsy, radiographs and LEMD3 testing to distinguish the connective-tissue naevi and bone foci from malignancy
Offer excision only where connective-tissue naevi are symptomatic or cosmetically troublesome
Document and monitor cutaneous lesions, including with clinical photography
Provide genetic counselling and family assessment given autosomal dominant inheritance with marked intrafamilial variability
